title: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
gist: GM will pay $220 million to settle with DC and 35 states over selling Smart Driver customer data to brokers who passed it to insurers. A third party must verify GM's compliance.

insights.claim: General Motors will pay $220 million to settle with the District of Columbia and 35 states whose attorneys general sued over its sale of Smart Driver customer data.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Connected-car data monetization now carries multi-state financial liability.

insights.claim: GM shared Smart Driver data with brokers who sold it to insurers, and some drivers saw higher premiums without knowing they had agreed to share the data.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Driver-behavior data feeding insurance pricing is a regulatory flashpoint for automakers and insurers.

insights.claim: A separate FTC settlement with GM and OnStar, finalized in January, bans sharing geolocation or driver behavior data with third parties for five years, and GM discontinued Smart Driver.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Automakers lose a data revenue stream and face stricter rules.

insights.claim: The state settlement requires a third party to verify GM's compliance with its privacy policy rather than accepting GM's word.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Independent audit requirements may become the template for other automakers.
